 News › News News › UP holiday list 2027: 27 public holidays notified, four-day Holi break, three-day Diwali break; full… UP holiday list 2027: 27 public holidays notified, four-day Holi break, three-day Diwali break; full official list with dates and days
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 08:00 IST UP announces list of school holidays for 2027 The Uttar Pradesh government has issued its official list of holidays for 2027. The notification was issued from Lucknow on November 17, 2026, by the General Administration Section, and it covers public holidays, restricted holidays, the annual closing of bank accounts and holidays declared under executive orders.
 In all, the state has notified 27 public holidays and 27 restricted holidays...
 Public holidays under the Negotiable Instruments Act 
 Twenty-six of the 27 public holidays fall under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. They are listed below with their days of the week:
 January: Makar Sankranti (14, Thursday) and Republic Day (26, Tuesday)
 February: Sant Ravidas Jayanti (20, Saturday)
 March: Mahashivratri (6, Saturday), Eid-ul-Fitr (10, Wednesday), Holika Dahan (22, Monday), Holi (23, Tuesday) and Good Friday (26, Friday)
 April: Dr B.R. Ambedkar Jayanti (14, Wednesday), Ram Navami (15, Thursday) and Mahavir Jayanti (19, Monday)
 May: Eid-uz-Zuha (17, Monday) and Buddha Purnima (20, Thursday)
 June: Muharram (16, Wednesday)
 August: Independence Day and Eid-e-Milad/Barawafat (15, Sunday), Raksha Bandhan (17, Tuesday) and Janmashtami (24, Tuesday)
 October: Gandhi Jayanti (2, Saturday), Dussehra Mahanavami (8, Friday), Vijayadashami (9, Saturday), Diwali (29, Friday), Govardhan Puja (30, Saturday) and Bhai Dooj/Chitragupt Jayanti (31, Sunday)
 November: Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima (14, Sunday)
 December: Hazrat Ali's birthday (12, Sunday) and Christmas Day (25, Saturday)
 The 27th public holiday is Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti on Friday, October 15. It is listed separately because it does not come under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Offices and educational institutions will be closed, but banks and financial institutions will stay open.
 Dates for Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-uz-Zuha, Muharram, Eid-e-Milad and Hazrat Ali's birthday will follow local moon sightings, so they may shift by a day.
 Four days off for Holi in 2027 
 Holika Dahan falls on Monday, March 22, and Holi on Tuesday, March 23. With Saturday, March 20, and Sunday, March 21, offices following a five-day week can enjoy a continuous break from March 20 to 23. Holi is also listed as a restricted holiday on Wednesday, March 24.
 Dussehra and Diwali holidays in 2027 
 Mahanavami (October 8) and Vijayadashami (October 9) fall on a Friday and a Saturday, producing a long weekend with Sunday. 
 Diwali on Friday, October 29, is followed by Govardhan Puja on Saturday and Bhai Dooj on Sunday, giving a three-day break. October has the most public holidays of any month, with seven.
 Weekend holidays in 2027 
 Six of the 27 public holidays fall on a Saturday and four on a Sunday: Sant Ravidas Jayanti, Mahashivratri, Gandhi Jayanti, Vijayadashami, Govardhan Puja and Christmas on Saturdays, and Independence Day, Bhai Dooj, Guru Nanak Jayanti and Hazrat Ali's birthday on Sundays.
 Restricted holidays in 2027 
 The 27 restricted holidays include New Year's Day (January 1), Basant Panchami (February 11), Easter Saturday and Easter Monday (March 27 and 29), Parshuram Jayanti (May 8), Maharana Pratap Jayanti (May 9), Anant Chaturdashi (September 14), Vishwakarma Puja (September 17), Narak Chaturdashi (October 28), Chhath Puja (November 4), Chaudhary Charan Singh's birthday (December 23) and Christmas Eve (December 24).
 Bank closing and executive-order holidays in 2027 
 The annual closing of accounts for commercial banks, applicable only to banks, treasuries and sub-treasuries, falls on Thursday, April 1. Two holidays have been declared under executive orders: Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti on Friday, January 15, and Guru Tegh Bahadur martyrdom day on Wednesday, November 24.
 Local holidays in 2027 
 District magistrates may declare up to three local holidays a year, informing the divisional commissioner at the start of each year with reasons. 
 Any additional local holiday requires prior government permission. In offices that follow a five-day week, executive-order holidays and local holidays declared by district magistrates do not apply.
 The notification sets holidays for government offices across the state. Schools and colleges publish their own academic calendars, and summer and winter vacations are usually notified separately, so families should confirm closures with their institutions.
